builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: The method replaces monolithic, latency-bound VLA inference with a decoupled design in which a large pretrained VLA proposes action chunks while a lightweight RL-fine-tuned edit policy reactively corrects actions using the latest observation. Costs include maintaining two models, RL fine-tuning infrastructure (based on EXPO-FT), online robot data collection, and the added system complexity of asynchronous chunk-plus-edit execution. Failures can arise if the edit policy overcorrects or destabilizes the VLA's behavior prior, if state observations remain noisy or delayed beyond what the edit policy can compensate for, or if the 10-minute online data budget proves insufficient for tasks with dynamics different from the four demonstrated.
rationale: The technique targets robotic manipulation with RL fine-tuning of pretrained VLA models, requiring physical robot hardware and an existing VLA checkpoint, so it is outside the typical LLM production scope and demands workload-specific validation before any adoption.
technique: RL fine-tuning of real-time VLA policies via action edits

claims.statement: The method replaces monolithic, latency-bound VLA inference with a decoupled design in which a large pretrained VLA proposes action chunks while a lightweight RL-fine-tuned edit policy reactively corrects actions using the latest observation. Costs include maintaining two models, RL fine-tuning infrastructure (based on EXPO-FT), online robot data collection, and the added system complexity of asynchronous chunk-plus-edit execution. Failures can arise if the edit policy overcorrects or destabilizes the VLA's behavior prior, if state observations remain noisy or delayed beyond what the edit policy can compensate for, or if the 10-minute online data budget proves insufficient for tasks with dynamics different from the four demonstrated.

On four dynamic real-world robot tasks with online data capped at 10 minutes, average policy success improved from 42% to 97%; on Kinetix it achieved the best delayed-policy performance in 10 of 10 environments.
